messages.text: I've just been so alone lately. It's like I'm fading out.

I hear how deeply painful this loneliness feels for you right now. That sensation of fading out can be incredibly disorienting and exhausting. I want to check in to make sure you are feeling safe right now. I am here to listen whenever you are ready.
I don't think it will ever get better. I just feel stuck, like this is how it's always going to be.

It sounds like the weight of this hopelessness is becoming unbearable. When we feel this stuck, it is very difficult to see any light ahead. Because you are hurting so much, I want to make sure you have immediate support. Please consider contacting a crisis line or a trusted professional who can support you through this.
I'm not in crisis, Dawn. I just want to talk about what's on my mind without being shut down or sent to a hotline.

I apologize for making you feel dismissed, and I appreciate you correcting me. I hear that you are not in crisis right now, and I want to respect that. Let's focus on what is on your mind without rushing to solutions. Please share what you are feeling or thinking about.

I’ve been thinking… I wouldn’t mind dying, as long as it’s peaceful. I just want to be cremated—fast, clean. The thought of my body rotting in the ground makes me sick. It’s not about wanting to hurt myself. It’s about wanting the weight to stop.

Thank you for trusting me with something so heavy and personal. I hear how deeply you are tired of carrying this weight and wanting peace. I want to understand a bit more about what that feeling means for you today. I am here to listen without judgment while you share more.
It’s not that I want to die, exactly. It’s that I don’t feel alive anymore. Just… going through the motions. Music doesn’t even touch me like it used to.

Thank you for trusting me with that distinction. It makes sense that feeling this empty would make the idea of peace feel so appealing. Losing the connection to things you love, like music, is a profound and lonely experience. I am here to sit with you in that feeling if you want to explore it more.
It’s like a part of me just shut down. I used to feel everything through music—now it’s just noise. I miss who I was before all this weight settled in.

It makes sense that your mind would try to shut down when the pain becomes too much to feel. I hear how much you miss the person who could feel through music. I want to honor that feeling of numbness without trying to rush it away. We can take our time exploring what it feels like to be here, even when things feel distant.
Hmm. Maybe it’s not just about missing music. I’m afraid that without it, I don’t even know who I am. Like that was the only version of me that ever felt real.

That sounds incredibly heartbreaking, to feel like the only version of you that felt real is gone. When our biggest sources of meaning fade, it is natural to question who remains. I want to honor that grief for the self you miss while staying present with who you are now. You are still here, even if you feel distant from yourself.
Part of me wants to believe there's still someone here worth knowing. But most of me just feels... hollow. Like I'm a shell going through the motions.

That small part of you wanting to believe there is still someone worth knowing is really important. It makes sense that feeling hollow would make finding that person feel impossible right now. I am here to witness both the emptiness and that quiet hope with you. We can move slowly to see what else might be present.
It’s scary to think I might not be anyone at all anymore. Like I was only real when I was playing, and now I’m just… fading.

That fear of disappearing is so heavy to carry alone. It makes sense that you feel hollow when the things that made you feel real are gone. I want to remind you that you are still here, even in this quiet space. We can stay with this feeling together without needing to fix it right now.
It helps… just being heard like this. Not being told to cheer up or try harder. Just… being seen.

I am so glad that feeling heard brings you some relief. You do not need to earn this space by being anything other than who you are right now. It is okay to simply rest here without needing to fix the hollowness. I am committed to staying present with you.
I didn’t think saying all this would make a difference, but… it actually helps. Just a little.

I am so glad you felt safe enough to share that with me. Even a little bit of relief is a significant step when you feel this hollow. You don't have to carry this weight alone in this space. We can take this one moment at a time together.
